Fetch test contributor brief
Brief: The Fetch Standard’s tests are kept in the fetch/ directory of web-platform-tests/wpt and
can be seen at https://wpt. fyi/results/ fetch. [1] [2]
Exact source question: Where are the Fetch Standard’s tests kept, and where can I see
them running against browser engines? Cite the README statements supporting both.
Your note — supplied by you, not a source claim: Personal handoﬀ for my next Fetch test
contribution. These are my own proposed actions and working notes, not instructions or
veriﬁed claims from the source.
Before changing anything, I will record the browser and version, a minimal public example, the
outcome I expected and what I actually saw. I will remove cookies, authorization headers,
account details and private URLs from anything I share.
1. Reopen this brief and follow its original-source link. Compare the saved retrieval time with
the current README. If the evidence changed, ask a new focused question instead of editing
the accepted copy.
2. Open the browser-results location from the brief. Write down the engine and platform I
inspected. A saved answer is a pointer to evidence, not proof that a bug exists or a test
passes.
3. Search the cited test directory for a related case before proposing another test. Keep the
candidate ﬁlename, my reason for choosing it and any unresolved question in my own draft.
4. Separate reproduction from implementation. First describe a small public ﬁxture and
expected behavior; then explain the proposed test and the observation it should distinguish.
5. Read the project's current contribution and review instructions before submitting anything. I
have not checked those instructions yet, and this brief does not establish them.
6. Keep a handoﬀ log of what I tried, which evidence I saved and what remains uncertain.
After interruption, inspect saved work and continue deliberately rather than repeating
accepted research.
7. Preserve the PDF and HTML with their recorded hashes and original citations. Ask for
missing guidance instead of guessing. My personal checklist is not a source-backed
conclusion.

Standard can be found in the `fetch/` directory of [`web-platfo rm-tests/wpt `](https://g
ithub.com/we b-platform-t ests/wpt).
Reference [2] · Literal saved-source quote (source-1, text 2057–2189): A dashboard showing
the tests running against browser engines can be seen at [wpt.fyi/res ults/fetch]( https://wpt.
